messages:
Aisha Khan: Heads up — we're seeing a sustained retry surge and pod load imbalance in west1-gpu pool. Traffic to svc/generate is landing mostly on pod-02 and pod-03 while pod-04..06 are idle. 30% errors from clients. Anyone on infra?
Tom Reed: investigating. Do we have ipvs or iptables mode on those nodes?
Aisha Khan: kube-proxy is in ipvs mode (confirmed). I pulled ipvsadm stats on node5:

```
ipvsadm -Ln --stats
TCP  10.244.1.120:443 rr
  -> 10.244.1.22:8080   Masq    100      3123456       0         0         0
  -> 10.244.1.23:8080   Masq     10      103456       0         0         0
  -> 10.244.1.24:8080   Masq      5       23456       0         0         0
```

Tom Reed: wow. weights are skewed (100 vs 10 vs 5) but we never set weights. Could be leftover connection pinning from prior endpoints.
Jia Park: ipvs session affinity uses timeout and can persist to a removed peer if conn table entries linger. What's conntrack count?
Aisha Khan: conntrack shows lots of ESTABLISHED entries to pod-02: 25k. I also see repeated SYN->RST on upstream from the client LB which triggers retries.
k8s-alert-bot: [alert] svc/generate retry-rate increased by 320% in west1-gpu in last 5m — https://redwood.tools/alerts/9876
Tom Reed: can you paste `kubectl get endpoints svc/generate -o json`? want to see endpoint ordering and readiness.
Aisha Khan: pasted output (trimmed):

```
"subsets": [
  { "addresses": [{"ip":"10.244.1.22"}], "notReadyAddresses": [] },
  { "addresses": [{"ip":"10.244.1.23"}], "notReadyAddresses": [] },
  { "addresses": [{"ip":"10.244.1.24"}], "notReadyAddresses": [] }
]
```

But that doesn't explain weight 100.
Jia Park: ipvs scheduling is per-svc and uses a local hash of endpoint weight table derived from kube-proxy's sync. If kube-proxy restarted with a different endpoint list and older conn entries persisted, you can get long-lived pinning. Also we've seen this when kube-proxy's endpoint slice ordering changed and we had per-node cache TTL mismatches.
Tom Reed: check /proc/net/ip_vs_conn and ip_vs_state timestamps. Also search kube-proxy logs for endpoint updates around the hour of the restart.
Aisha Khan: found kube-proxy log on node5 — repeated reconcile failures at 03:12 UTC, then a restart at 03:13. After restart ipvs still had old conn entries: conn_count shows many entries with 'expires' > 3600.
oncall-bot: @Aisha Khan, I created a temporary mitigation: toggled svc externalTrafficPolicy and rolled kube-proxy as a canary on 2 nodes. Please monitor.
Tom Reed: mitigation good. Long-term fix: reduce ipvs session timeout, ensure kube-proxy carries endpoint slice versions in its state so reconciliation doesn't create ghost weights, and add a cleanup on startup to flush ip_vs_conn when endpoint sets change dramatically.
Jia Park: also consider enabling endpoint-hash-randomization in kube-proxy and ensure consistent hostname ordering. For GPU pools with sticky traffic patterns (long streams), we should also use an L4 reverse-proxy with active health checks so ipvs doesn't pin to unhealthy pods.
Aisha Khan: rolling kube-proxy across west1 completed. Retry rate dropped ~75% and load distribution looks even now. Will open an RFC for the kube-proxy startup cleanup and lowering the ipvs timeout for GPU service classes.
Tom Reed: thx. capture any postmortem data and include a short playbook for oncall (how to detect ipvs pinning + quick flush commands).
Aisha Khan: will do. initial postmortem to follow.
